proposal: The Mandate says a conservative administration should include a citizenship question in the decennial census, relying on the Supreme Court's 2019 holding that the Commerce Secretary has broad authority to add one. It also recommends reviewing the planned race and ethnicity question changes and all decennial and American Community Survey questions, auditing 2030 census planning and budgets, and abolishing the Census Bureau's National Advisory Committee while reevaluating, and potentially abolishing, its other non-statutory standing committees. Topics are due to Congress by April 1, 2027 and questions by April 1, 2028.

status_summary: The Census Bureau's advisory committees (including the National Advisory Committee) are no longer operating; its website says as of its August 2026 revision that it has no advisory committees, after meetings were cancelled in March 2025. A Federal Register notice of 2026-02-03 (91 FR 4864) announced the submission to OMB for a 2026 operational test, and the notice itself does not mention citizenship, while NPR reported that the filing indicated respondents may be asked about it (OMB approval of that item was not confirmed). On 2026-09-10 the Bureau proposed rules (91 FR 57524) that would count only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents toward apportionment (other foreign nationals, including people in the country illegally and those with temporary or indefinite status, would not be counted), invite comment on adding a legal-status question to the short form, and bar race, ethnicity and sexual-orientation questions from the enumeration form; the comment period now runs to 2026-11-02. The proposal does not itself add a citizenship question, and no 2030 questions have been finalized.

timeline.event: The Census Bureau publishes Federal Register notices (dated 2025-03-10 through 2025-03-13) cancelling meetings of the Census Scientific Advisory Committee, the 2030 Census Advisory Committee and the National Advisory Committee. The Bureau later states it has no advisory committees.

Census Bureau notice (91 FR 4864) of its submission to OMB of the information collection for the 2026 Operational Test in Support of the 2030 Census (OMB control 0607-0936; about 154,600 respondents in Spartanburg, South Carolina and Huntsville, Alabama; internet self-response and in-field enumeration).

Proposed rule 'Decennial Census of the Population of Americans' (91 FR 57524) would add 15 CFR parts 60 and 70: residence criteria counting only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents toward apportionment, a request for comment on a short-form legal-status question, and limits on demographic questions (sex, date of birth and household relationships allowed; race, ethnicity and sexual orientation barred).
The Census Bureau extends the comment period on the proposed rule from 2026-10-13 to 2026-11-02 (91 FR 63207).

title: Add a citizenship question to the census and reshape Census Bureau operations
uncertainties: Could not confirm whether OMB approved the citizenship item in the 2026 test; the 2026-02-03 notice (91 FR 4864) was read in review and does not state whether a citizenship item is included, so that claim rests on NPR reporting. The date and exact wording of the President's August 2025 call for a new census are known only through NPR's later reporting, and the two NPR reports are kept as sources rather than timeline events because they are not government actions. Formal termination of the National Advisory Committee is inferred from the Bureau's page (revised 2026-08-12, stating it has no advisory committees) and the March 2025 meeting cancellation notices, which were not opened. A Federal Register listing of Census Bureau documents (first 40 titles, newest first) showed no final rule on the residence criteria, only the 2026-10-05 comment extension, and a notice on 2030 Census communications research (2026-10-05) that was not opened. The proposed rule cites pending state suits, including Louisiana v. Department of Commerce (W.D. La., filed 2025-01-17) and Missouri v. Department of Commerce (E.D. Mo., filed 2026-01-30), over the 2020 residence criteria; a litigation tracker (Democracy Docket, a lead only) describes the Louisiana case as paused since 2025-03-06 with a status hearing set for 2026-11-10; no court filing was opened and no court challenge to the September 2026 proposed rule was found. Stage judgment: the advisory committee element is operative, while the central citizenship element is only a request for comment in a proposed rule, so the record sits at the bottom of in_progress; proposed at about 20 is the other defensible call.
